text: Metrics are numbers over time. Logs are detailed, structured or unstructured records of events, and they need somewhere to live before you can search them — a Log Analytics workspace, a container that stores log data collected from VMs, diagnostic settings on other resources, and services like Microsoft Sentinel or Defender for Cloud, so it can all be queried together in one place rather than hunting through each resource individually.

You search that data with KQL, Kusto Query Language, written top to bottom and piped with the pipe character as it filters and summarizes. This query pulls every successful Azure Resource Manager operation from the last 24 hours and counts them by operation type. It's worth pausing on: this exact query language also powers Microsoft Sentinel, the cloud SIEM you'll meet again in the Cybersecurity path, so learning to read it here pays off twice.

The Activity Log is a different kind of record entirely — not a metric, not part of Log Analytics by default. It's automatically enabled for every subscription at no extra cost, and it captures control-plane operations: administrative actions against the same Azure Resource Manager from Chapter 1. For each one it logs who did it (the caller's identity), what operation ran, when it happened, and whether it succeeded or failed.

Say a VM is suddenly stopped and nobody admits to it. A metric chart shows the VM is off, nothing more. The Activity Log shows exactly which account ran the stop operation and at what timestamp — filtered by resource in the portal, or as a KQL query if that log has been routed into a workspace, retained 90 days by default either way.

Between metrics and the Activity Log, you now know what's happening and who caused it. The piece still missing is getting notified automatically instead of checking by hand. Next up: alert rules and action groups — the condition-and-action pair that turns a threshold into an email, a text, or an automated response.
